faq.heading: FAQ
faq.q1: What can and can't it do?
faq.a1: You can open artifacts you made with AI, such as slides and documents, in an editor in your own browser, fix them and save them. It is a tool for one person on one machine, not a shared service. The supported editors and environments will be listed here once they are checked on the released version.
faq.q2: Where is my data saved? How do I back it up?
faq.a2: Saved artifacts and their history stay in a data folder on your machine (for example ~/.local/share/EditorPlatform/ClaudeCode on Linux). To back up, close Claude Code and the editor, then copy the whole folder somewhere safe.
faq.q3: How do I update or remove it?
faq.a3: Use Claude Code's plugin update and uninstall commands. Uninstalling keeps the data folder, so delete it separately after a backup if you want it gone. Exact steps will appear in Get started at release.
faq.a4: Claude Code must be allowed to use plugins and MCP (your organization's policy must permit it). The plugin listens only inside your own machine and opens no public endpoint.
faq.q5: What does the AI host receive?
faq.a5: Saving locally does not mean nothing is sent to AI. When an artifact is read, created, changed by a proposal or exported, its saved content goes to Claude Code and its model provider. Unsaved edits are not sent. The plugin itself calls no AI service.
faq.a6: The plugin itself needs no sign-in or API key. Using Claude Code requires your own Claude Code plan.
faq.note: These answers are based on the pre-release candidate and will be checked again at release.
